P001.name: pareval_03_dense_la_axpy
P001.description:
BLAS-1 AXPY: z = alpha * x + y elementwise.

Each output element is computed independently. Results should match
the reference to within a few ULPs — small last-bit differences from
FMA contraction (GPU's `fma(a,x,y)` rounds once; CPU's `a*x+y` rounds
twice) are tolerated by the checker.

Binary I/O:
  argv[1] = input.bin   [int32 N][double alpha][double x[N]][double y[N]]
  argv[2] = output.bin  [double z[N]]

gen_input.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Random doubles in [-1, 1], scalar alpha drawn from same range."""
import argparse, random, struct
from pathlib import Path

def gen(N, seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    alpha = rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0)
    x = [rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0) for _ in range(N)]
    y = [rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0) for _ in range(N)]
    return (struct.pack("<i", N)
            + struct.pack("<d", alpha)
            + struct.pack(f"<{N}d", *x)
            + struct.pack(f"<{N}d", *y))

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--N",     type=int, default=8192)
    ap.add_argument("--seed",  type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--count", type=int, default=10)
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="./inputs")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out_dir); out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for i in range(args.count):
        s = args.seed + i
        f = out / f"input_{i}.bin"
        f.write_bytes(gen(args.N, s))
        print(f"wrote {f}: N={args.N}, seed={s}, {f.stat().st_size} bytes")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

P002.name: pareval_18_graph_count_components
P002.description:
Count the number of connected components in an undirected graph. Input is an NxN adjacency matrix (symmetric, no self-loops). Binary I/O contract:
  argv[1] = input.bin   [int32 N][int32 A[N*N]]
  argv[2] = output.bin  [int32 result]

gen_input.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate random input.bin files for 18_graph_count_components.

Binary format (matches the contract in main.cpp):
    [int32 N]
    [int32 A[N*N]]   row-major adjacency, symmetric, A[i*N+i]=0

Defaults are tuned so the graph is interesting — N=512 with p≈0.005
sits a bit below the Erdős-Rényi connectivity threshold ln(N)/N,
giving a handful of components (not 1, not N).

Usage:
    uv run --no-project python3 gen_input.py
    uv run --no-project python3 gen_input.py --count 10
    uv run --no-project python3 gen_input.py --N 1024 --p 0.003 --count 10
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import random
import struct
from pathlib import Path


def gen_random_undirected(N: int, p_edge: float, seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    A = [0] * (N * N)
    for i in range(N):
        for j in range(i + 1, N):
            if rng.random() < p_edge:
                A[i * N + j] = 1
                A[j * N + i] = 1
    return struct.pack("<i", N) + struct.pack(f"<{N*N}i", *A)


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--N",     type=int,   default=512)
    ap.add_argument("--p",     type=float, default=0.005,
                    help="Edge probability (default 0.005, ~ ln(N)/N for N=512).")
    ap.add_argument("--seed",  type=int,   default=42,
                    help="Base seed; case i uses seed+i (default 42).")
    ap.add_argument("--count", type=int,   default=1,
                    help="Number of cases to generate (default 1).")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="./inputs",
                    help="Output directory (default ./inputs).")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    out_dir = Path(args.out_dir)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    for i in range(args.count):
        seed = args.seed + i
        payload = gen_random_undirected(args.N, args.p, seed)
        out = out_dir / f"input_{i}.bin"
        out.write_bytes(payload)
        print(f"wrote {out}: N={args.N}, p={args.p}, seed={seed}, "
              f"{len(payload)} bytes")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Random ints in [0, value_max]; target chosen so half cases hit, half miss."""
import argparse, random, struct
from pathlib import Path

def gen(N, value_max, seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    x = [rng.randint(0, value_max) for _ in range(N)]
    # Alternate target presence by seed parity to exercise both branches
    if seed % 2 == 0:
        target = rng.choice(x)             # guaranteed hit
    else:
        target = value_max + 1 + (seed % 7)  # guaranteed miss (out of range)
    return (struct.pack("<i", N)
            + struct.pack("<i", target)
            + struct.pack(f"<{N}i", *x))

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--N",        type=int, default=20000)
    ap.add_argument("--value-max",type=int, default=1000)
    ap.add_argument("--seed",     type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--count",    type=int, default=10)
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir",  default="./inputs")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out_dir); out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for i in range(args.count):
        s = args.seed + i
        f = out / f"input_{i}.bin"
        f.write_bytes(gen(args.N, args.value_max, s))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate input.bin for hecbench_accuracy (P005).

Default scaled-down: N=128 rows, D=64 columns, top_k=5.
"""
import argparse
import random
import struct
from pathlib import Path


def gen(N: int, D: int, top_k: int, seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    X = [rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0) for _ in range(N * D)]

            + struct.pack("<i", top_k)

            + struct.pack(f"<{N}i", *labels))

P021.description:
Compute a BFS shortest-path tree rooted at vertex 0 in an undirected unweighted graph (NxN adjacency matrix). For each vertex v output parent[v], where parent[0] = -1 (source), parent[v] = -2 if v is unreachable, and otherwise parent[v] is SOME predecessor u with dist[u] + 1 == dist[v]. The tree is NOT UNIQUE — when v has multiple equidistant predecessors, any valid choice is acceptable.

  argv[2] = output.bin  [int32 parent[N]]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Random undirected graph generator for bfs_shortest_path_tree.

Default N=100, p=0.05 — dense enough that vertices commonly have multiple
equidistant predecessors, exercising the non-unique-answer property of
BFS trees.
"""
import argparse
import random
import struct
from pathlib import Path


def gen_random_undirected(N, p, seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    A = [0] * (N * N)
    for i in range(N):
        for j in range(i + 1, N):
            if rng.random() < p:
                A[i * N + j] = 1
                A[j * N + i] = 1
    return struct.pack("<i", N) + struct.pack(f"<{N*N}i", *A)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--N",     type=int,   default=100)
    ap.add_argument("--p",     type=float, default=0.05)
    ap.add_argument("--seed",  type=int,   default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--count", type=int,   default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="./inputs")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out_dir); out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for i in range(args.count):
        seed = args.seed + i
        payload = gen_random_undirected(args.N, args.p, seed)
        f = out / f"input_{i}.bin"
        f.write_bytes(payload)
        print(f"wrote {f}: N={args.N}, p={args.p}, seed={seed}, {len(payload)} bytes")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Generate input.bin for sort_by_key_with_ties (P006).

P030.description:
Return any K indices that select the K largest values of the
input. The output indices must be sorted ascending. When the
K-th boundary value has ties, multiple valid index sets exist;
the checker accepts any subset that captures the same multiset
of top-K values.

Binary I/O:
  argv[1] = input.bin   [int32 N][int32 K][double values[N]]
  argv[2] = output.bin  [int32 indices[K]]   (sorted ascending)

gen_input.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""original_top_k_indices — values drawn from a small range to force ties."""
import argparse, random, struct
from pathlib import Path

def gen(N, K, seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Draw from a moderate range so ties at the K-th boundary are
    # plausible — exercises the multi-valid property of the checker.
    vals = [float(rng.randint(0, 50)) for _ in range(N)]
    return (struct.pack("<i", N) + struct.pack("<i", K)
            + struct.pack(f"<{N}d", *vals))

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--N", type=int, default=2000)
    ap.add_argument("--K", type=int, default=20)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--count", type=int, default=10)
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="./inputs")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out_dir); out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for i in range(args.count):
        s = args.seed + i
        f = out / f"input_{i}.bin"
        f.write_bytes(gen(args.N, args.K, s))
        print(f"wrote {f}: N={args.N}, K={args.K}, seed={s}, {f.stat().st_size} bytes")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
